pr_title: [Blazor] Try to load the assembly when finding out a root component or a parameter in webassembly
pr_body:
# Load assembly when finding root component or parameter in WebAssembly

This change allows the system to load the assembly when a root component is defined in an RCL and rendered in WebAssembly, even if the assembly is not yet loaded into memory.

## Description

When a root component is defined in an RCL and rendered in WebAssembly, it might happen that the assembly for the component is not yet loaded into memory if the app has not used any type from the dll.
This causes the framework to fail finding the assembly when it tries to look for it in the list of loaded assemblies.

The fix is to detect this in webassembly and try to load the root component type at that point. Same with the component parameters.

Fixes #52129

## Customer Impact

A Blazor Web app may experience a failure trying to render a root component in WebAssembly, when the component is defined in a Razor Class Library. This will happen if the assembly containing the component hasn't yet been loaded on the client, and the app is trying to render that component.

## Regression?

- [ ] Yes
- [x] No

## Risk

- [ ] High
- [ ] Medium
- [x] Low

The assembly will already be downloaded by JS and is ready to be loaded.

## Verification

- [x] Manual (required)
- [x] Automated

There was manual verification that the fix addressed the issue and it was automated into an E2E test.

## Packaging changes reviewed?

- [ ] Yes
- [ ] No
- [x] N/A

There are no packaging changes associated with this fix.

## When servicing release/2.1

- [ ] Make necessary changes in eng/PatchConfig.props

> My only question is about the debugging experience in the case where there's an assembly loading error. Will leave it with you to decide whether it's already ideal or could be made clearer by letting the exception be thrown.

I'm fine leaving it as is (you'll get the same experience you get today), since this is typically a "build up" issue, that happens as you start growing your app. In pretty much every app, you are going to actually reference the assembly types in code explicitly, for example to register services, etc.

So I think this is a point in time issue during dev that just happens when you add the first component and try to render it.

This was/is likely also present in previous webassembly versions, we just didn't make it easy to prerender.

> I'm fine leaving it as is (you'll get the same experience you get today), since this is typically a "build up" issue, that happens as you start growing your app. In pretty much every app, you are going to actually reference the assembly types in code explicitly, for example to register services, etc.

To be honest I don't quite get this. Even during this "build up" phase, won't it be easier to understand and fix the `Assembly.Load` failure if we allow it to throw? What's the advantage of intentionally suppressing the exception so that a different error occurs later?

> To be honest I don't quite get this. Even during this "build up" phase, won't it be easier to understand and fix the Assembly.Load failure if we allow it to throw? What's the advantage of intentionally suppressing the exception so that a different error occurs later?

How can this error happen?

> How can this error happen?

I don't know, but if it can't, why did you add a try/catch?

> I don't know, but if it can't, why did you add a try/catch?

Because in case it happens, it doesn't change the existing experience, so the fix is more scoped. Thinking hard, the only case where I think this can happen is:
1) The assembly is lazy loaded (there's a separate bug tracking that fix [here](https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/issues/26601)).
2) The assembly is not referenced by the client application at all. (Like you forgot to add the project reference).

In both cases you'll end up with the current error message that tells you that the assembly couldn't be found, which I think it's better than whatever `Assembly.Load` could throw if it fails.

If I'm reading the code correctly, if we suppress the assembly loading exception, the error message will say:

 > Root component type '{registeredComponent.TypeName}' could not be found in the assembly '{registeredComponent.Assembly}'.  This is likely a result of trimming (tree shaking).");

That's a bit of a weird message because the phrasing implies that the assembly is known, but the type wasn't in it (likely due to trimming). It would be more informative to say the assembly as a whole cannot be loaded, so people don't spend hours trying to change trimmer config when that's actually nothing to do with the problem. I don't know exactly what exception messages can come out of `Assembly.Load` but if it was something like `Failed to load MyCompany.MyAssembly: bad image format` that would convey far more useful information that implying a type was missing from the assembly. And then people will only get the error that says "likely a result of trimming" if the assembly *was* loaded but the type was missing from it.

Sorry to be going on about this. I know it's not really a high priority and really will accept whatever you decide here, without further comment on this point. I already approved the PR. Please do whatever you feel is best!

issue_context.title: RenderMode not working with razor class libraries
issue_context.body:
### Is there an existing issue for this?

- [X] I have searched the existing issues

### Describe the bug

When I create a project that has a razor class library and I try to use this code
@rendermode InteractiveAuto
and try to compile that library, it always fails to compile because does not know anything about @rendermode

Works fine when using under blazorwebapp.
However, some cases i need razor class library so I can share with blazor hybrid and use other places as well.


### Expected Behavior

The expected behavior is for the project to compile and run.
When using web, then do as promised on the counter where it first uses blazor server and the next time web assembly (since the components would have been downloaded).


### Steps To Reproduce

1.  Create blank solution
2.  Create blazor web app
3. Create maui blazor hybrid
4. Create shared library
5. Move the Counter from blazor web app client to the shared
6. Make the necessary changes necessary including referencing the proper projects and putting in the additional assemblies
7. Run
8. Will always fail to load (even the blazor web app).

### Exceptions (if any)

Severity	Code	Description	Project	File	Line	Suppression State
Error (active)	CS0103	The name 'InteractiveAuto' does not exist in the current context




### .NET Version

8

### Anything else?

_No response_

@apocalipisis, what might be happening in your case is a component with an interactive render mode is attempting to render a child component with a different interactive render mode. This is not supported. For example, it won't work if you have an app with root-level server interactivity and you try to render a component with an `InteractiveWebAssembly` render mode. For more information, refer to our docs on this topic: https://learn.microsoft.com/aspnet/core/blazor/components/render-modes?view=aspnetcore-8.0#render-mode-propagation.
The only issue left is does not work with a maui app though.

@musictopia2, if a render mode is specified in a component's definition, it's effectively saying, "This component requires 'x' type of interactivity". Blazor Hybrid is a different technology than Blazor Server or Blazor WebAssembly, so a component that requires Server/WebAssembly interactivity won't work in a Blazor Hybrid app.

Unless a component is designed to _only_ work with Server or WebAssembly interactivity, the interactive render mode should be specified at the call site instead. For example, instead of:

_MyComponent.razor:_
```razor
@rendermode InteractiveAuto
...
```

...do this:

_Index.razor_
```razor
<MyComponent @rendermode="InteractiveAuto" />
```

For more info, see the note in the docs [here](https://learn.microsoft.com/aspnet/core/blazor/components/render-modes?view=aspnetcore-8.0#apply-a-render-mode-to-a-component-definition).

@SongPing, if you need to have an interactive page in a Razor Class library, there are a few options:
1. Push interactivity up a layer. This is referred to as "app level" interactivity, and it involves making the `Routes` component interactive. It does, however, mean that interactivity might be enabled for pages that don't necessarily need it.
2. Push component interactivity down a layer. This is similar to what you did in your workaround.
3. Come up with a custom mechanism to select page interactivity. I wrote a gist here to show an example of this [here](https://gist.github.com/MackinnonBuck/441681764d879d9ac4906aaec6410eb9).
